desirous of Krishna, desiring the favour of Krishna's love, welfare, of sweet speech, by her brow's illusion, very auspicious,

treasury of love's sport, adorned with ear-ornaments on cheeks, lovely with the radiance of a golden mountain, first in love, languid with intoxication,
thinking of Krishna, thinking of love, thinking of passion, giving Krishna; thinking of Rasa, thinking of feeling, pure thoughts, of great Rasa,
for whom the blink of an eye without seeing Krishna is an age, rebuker of the lashes of the eyes, mother of Kandarpa, chief, giver of the way to Vaikuntha,
of the feeling of Rasa, embraced by her beloved, dearest, first heroine, pure-bodied, Rama, bud of Rasa,
of great influence, of good conduct, the golden river, Narmada's mother, Gomati, praised by Chandrabhaga, Sarayu, the Tamraparni (rivers) in her form,
of stainless character, without qualities and without stain. This thousand-fold list of names of the form of the Pair, O Narada,
is to be recited with effort by one who longs for the sentiment of Vrindavana: it quells great sins, removes barrenness,
removes poverty, destroys disease, grants desires greatly, removes sin, destroys enemies, and gives devotion to Radha and Madhava.
Homage to that Lord Krishna, of unfailing intelligence; homage to him who ever sports in the ocean of nectar of Radha's company.
The goddess Radha is the maker of the world, intent on preserving the world, the ordainer of the world's dissolution, the Lady of all, the mother of all.
Her thousand names I have told, O lord of sages, divine, giving enjoyment and liberation; what more do you wish to hear?
Now I shall tell you the rite of Mahalakshmi, O Narada, by whose worship the practitioner would become one who has both enjoyment and liberation.
Lakshmi, Maya, Kama, Vani first; "Kamalavasini" in the dative; ending "vahnipriya": this is another best wish-granting tree of mantra.
Its sage is Narayana, the metre Jagati; the deity is Mahalakshmi; the six limbs are made with pairs of syllables.
She is bright as white champaka, adorned with jewelled ornaments, with a gentle smile and gracious face, eager to favour devotees,
bearing a jewelled garland, bright as ten million moons. Having meditated thus, he should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth with milk-rice,
in a kindled fire; he should worship with the Shri-sight... on the seat joined with the nine powers, with the limbs and enclosures.
Vibhuti, Unnati, Kanti, Srishti, Kirti, Sannati, Vyashti, Utkrishti, Riddhi: these are the nine powers declared.
Invoking and conceiving the form with the root, the practitioner should worship the six limbs in the six corners; on the right the elephant-faced one (Ganesha),
on the left the flower-bowed one (Kama); then on the eight petals: Uma, Shri, Bharati, Durga, Dharani, the Veda-mother,
Devi Usha in the east and the others, in the directions and corners in order; Ganga and Yamuna are to be worshipped as washing the feet;
the conch and lotus treasures are to be worshipped at the sides, holding ghee and chowries; then in the west Varuna holding an umbrella.
Having worshipped the signs of the zodiac and the nine planets in their places, he should worship the elephants such as Airavata with four tusks in the directions and corners;
outside them the guardians of the world and their weapons. A man for long life should offer durva soaked in ghee.
One who offers guduchi soaked in ghee for seven days and a thousand and eight times lives a hundred autumns.
Having offered sesame smeared with ghee, he gains long life. From a Sunday, the mantra-knower should offer for ten days, soaked in ghee,
arka fuel-sticks for accomplishing health of the body. One who daily offers a thousand and eight with rice-grains
soon surely gets great prosperity. With dust of ... mixed with ghee,
he should offer a hundred and eight, eating milk-rice daily; within a circle even he becomes like Kubera.
By an offering of jaggery-mixed oblation he becomes rich in food; he should offer a thousand and eight hibiscus flowers.
The best Brahmin should make a tilaka of that ash mixed with betel juice for bewildering the four classes.
The best of practitioners who thus worships Lakshmi, O lord of sages, gets prosperity; Mahalakshmi is pleased.
At the body's end he surely obtains Vishnu's abode. Durga, O best of Brahmins, who as Sati went to Shiva's world,
by Shiva's order made a divine world known as Devi-loka, unlike all worlds.
Staying there, the mother of the world, observing austerity and vows, constantly makes various incarnations of herself at the three times.
Maya, higher, joined with Hladini, with the moon, again with visarga, Pratishtha with Smriti, again with Kshudha,
Jnanamrita, Vahnijaya: with Om at the start this mantra is declared. Its sage is Vamadeva; the metre Gayatri is declared;
the deity is Durga, the origin of the worlds, destroyer of misfortune. The heart and the other two limbs are conceived with Om and each letter.
With three, the armour; with two, the eye; with all, the weapon is declared. He should meditate on Goddess Durga, like a great emerald, adorned with a thousand arms,
bearing various weapons, three-eyed, moon-crested, rich in bracelets, armlets and necklaces, with tinkling anklets,
wearing crown and earrings.
He should chant the mantra eight hundred thousand and offer with sesame and honey; or a thousand with milk-rice; he should worship on the nine-lotus figure.
Prabha, Maya, Jaya, Sukshma, Vishuddha, Nandini, Suprabha, Vijaya, Sarvasiddhida are the powers of the seat.
With water, without the three short vowels and the neuter, he should worship these. Om, "Vajranakha-damshtrayudhaya mahapada"...
Simhaya, armour, weapon, heart: the Lion mantra is declared, O sage. With it he should give the seat and conceive the form from the root.
Having first worshipped the enclosure of limbs, he should worship the powers on the petals: Jaya, Vijaya, Kirti, Priti, then Prabha again,
Shraddha, Medha, Shruti, with their own names beginning with the initial letters; on the petal-tips he should worship in order the eight weapons:
conch, discus, mace, sword, noose, goad, arrow, bow; then outside, the lords of the worlds and then their weapons.
Thus by chanting and the rest, when the mantra is perfected, the one who knows the rite may perform applications for each of his own desires.
Having established nine lovely pots by rule, joined with jewels, gold and the like, set in the nine vessels,
he should worship the Goddess in the middle one, Jaya and the others in the rest. Having worshipped with perfume, flowers and the like, he should consecrate the king.
The king conquers his enemies and gains the glory of victory; he who is sick gets long life, free of all disease.
A barren woman, sprinkled by rule, obtains an excellent son. Ghee chanted over with this mantra removes minor evil planets;
especially for pregnant women, ash and the like chanted over. In yawning and breathing... Krishna's entering...
The Goddess who arose holding lute and book — hear, O best of Brahmins, her rite, beneficial to the world.
Om, Vagbhava (aim), Maya, Shri, Kama, Shakti are said; "Sarasvatyai" in the dative, ending in "svaha": a twelve-syllable mantra.
Narayana is its sage; the metre Virat is declared; Mahasarasvati is its deity.
Having made the six limbs with the Vagbhava seed, the wise should place the letters: Om at the Brahma-aperture; Lajja between the brows;
at the face, nose and ears, and at the lower openings, the syllables beginning "shri". Then he should meditate on the goddess of speech holding lute and book,
white as camphor and jasmine, with a face radiant as the full moon, seated on a swan, adorned with a moon on the forehead and divine ornaments.
He should chant twelve hundred thousand and offer a thousand with white lotuses, or with naga and champaka flowers, the best practitioner.
He should worship her on the alphabet seat as told, in the order to be stated. He should give the seat with the lotus of letters and conceive the form with the root.
To the right of the goddess, the refined, speech-made, auspicious one is to be worshipped; to the left the natural one, speech-made, giver of all success.
First the limbs, then in the six corners; outside: Prajna and the rest: Prajna, Medha, Shruti, Shakti, Smriti, Vagishvari, Mati,
and Svasti — so they are called; then Brahma and the rest; again he should worship the lords of the world and then their weapons outside.
Having thus worshipped the Goddess of Speech, he himself becomes a lord of speech: celibate, pure, with clean teeth and nails,
remembering all women as goddesses always, the wise one surely gains poetic power in twelve months.
Drinking water consecrated by that mantra a thousand times daily, O sage, the mantra-knower becomes a great poet in a year, without doubt.
Standing in water up to the chest, meditating on the Goddess seated in the disc of the sun, he should chant the mantra three thousand times daily;
within a circle he gains success and incomparable speech on earth. Offering palasha and bilva flowers sprinkled with honey,
or with fuel-sticks from them, he gains the fame of the Lord of Speech; with flowers from the royal tree soaked in sweet things...
